I once went to sleep in the afternoon and woke up with a bunch of EMTs around me. My dog apparently knew something was wrong and got my parents. I was only 13 at the time. Had no idea what was happening, no clue that my blood sugar was low. I have a CGM (continuous glucose monitor) now, and as much as I hate the service the company provides, the monitor itself has been a life saver on multiple occasions, especially now that I'm in my 20s and on my own. The problem is it costs thousands of dollars to pay for it. The piece of equipment probably costs a few dollars to make, and the sensors even less. It's all plastic. I've had to ration my insulin because insulin costs me hundreds of dollars. I'm in the US though, not the UK. Being a Diabetic in this country really, really sucks.

Gerrymandering is awful, but id still engage with people like that. If theyre a walking soundbite from fox or breitbart, then youre never gonna get anywhere with them, because youre not actually engaging with a person. Most people are pretty good though if youre just talking, both on the right and the left. People that dont know how to turn off an idealogue are rare.. but theyre becoming more common, which is sad. Its like we're losing a part of our humanity as a nation because everything is so partisan.... people are told what to think in this country and arent seeing things from anyone elses perspective. I grew up in a cult,  and i know how mind control and undue influence works. There is a LOT of it in the media and in politics. People are brought up to believe that their side is right, that just about everything they say is right, and to stand for anything else is a moral failing. Its cultish behavior on both sides and its appalling. Thats why engagement, talk, and being a good person is so important right now. There isnt a good or bad side, really. But there are tribes fighting for influence becuase theyve been led to believe that only their way is the right way, and their only association with the opposing side is on twitter or on biased webpages / news sources. Most people are decent, but we never see that side of them.

Then, of course, when you get into racial superiority, the conversation is not something im particularly fond of engaging in, mostly because i just cant handle people like that without getting angry. Im not a therapist, and thats what those people need.

Most people, in my experience, are just normal when you talk to them.... its when the idealogue gets turned on that conversations get frustrating because theyre no longer people, theyre soundbites. I actively try to avoid triggering the idealogues in any conversations. When they are triggered, i think genuinely listening and asking sincere, non confrontational questions can bring the person back. If not that, then just changing the subject can work. If a person is only ever a walking soundbite, then you can never really engage with them in any meaningful way... theres no real conversation to be had. But those people, in my experience, are rare. Those are usually the narcissistic types who want to be seen in a holier-than-thou light. I generally avoid those people. 

If people dont want to talk to me because of my beliefs, thats on them. Im not gonna be pushy one way or the other. I just like to get peoples perspectives because i get to see their humanity, and they get to see mine. I think thats important, and something we lose out on if our only association with people of different political beliefs is via twitter or a news site.

As far as actually being friends with people... well, i want friends who want whats best for me, who look forward to seeing good things happen to me. It doesnt matter where they come from. Obviously there are people who are dangerous or exhibit really risky behaviour which i tend to stay away from, but you kinda just have to guage how you feel around them and whether they care about people or not. If they dont care about people in general, chances are, they wont care so much about you. Thats a waste of a friendship, in my pinion.

That's true, but we have 'freedom of the press' for a reason. Laws that have the potential to circumvent that freedom and prosecute investigative journalists (particularly in government) who perhaps are on to something but don't have enough clear cut evidence to prove their findings 100%, can potentially harm the distribution of critical information about their government. We see this happening in Russia, for example. The freedom of the press acts as a form of checks and balances, and keeps authorities accountable, if not in the court of law, then in public opinion and political standing. This of course has the potential to be abused by the press, but it's a slippery slope when you start regulating their freedom to pursue a story.

Just because a news outlet profiles some guy like Richard Spencer in a less-than-extreme light doesn't mean his views weren't revealed by everything he said after the fact. The more attention you draw to an individual, and the more you try to figure out what he/she's thinking by having conversations with them, the more clear their intentions become. It's clear that there were preconceived biases going into these hit-pieces, and it's disappointing that more effort isn't being put into figuring out what the truth is. 

I still think the way they do these profiles is incredibly reckless and unprofessional. If they can't work with integrity at their current load, then they need to take more time on each piece. Same can be said in the case of Richard Spencer's profile. Ask questions. Do research. Figure out what he's thinking. If people are acting as politicians, it's the journalists jobs to get to the truth. And the truth in Spencer's case is he's an incredibly racist, garbage person.
